title: Research: exact five-call minimum for binary tetrahedral mixed triple (no new kappa)
body:
## Result

Adds `research/sl2f3-conjugate-triple-seed592f/`, a scoped exact result in the full formal algebra `F2[SL2(F3)]`. For the three-role target `diag([i],[w],[w^-1 i w])` and four address labels `{i,i^-1,w,w^-1}`, the exact paid-call minimum is five. The separate direct word costs five; exhaustive exact coverage excludes every four-call-or-shorter word. This is a negative result for one new nonabelian alphabet, not a new `kappa` or supplier construction.

## Exact model and evidence

The group has order 24, generated by the pinned matrices `i=[[0,1],[-1,0]]` and `w=[[0,-1],[1,-1]]` over `F3`. The paid factor is `D_N(g)=I+([g]+[e])N` for each of the 28 binary rank-one idempotents in `M3(F2)`, giving 112 paid factors. Free scalar `GL3(F2)` mixing is included by augmentation/conjugation closure. Every paid factor costs one.

The verifier covers all lengths 0 through 4. The 12,544 ordered two-call words collapse to 8,905 exact states; each distinct state is checked as a suffix against the complete prefix set for both 1+2 and 2+2 splits. This exhausts all 1,404,928 length-three and 157,351,936 length-four raw words, as well as shorter lengths. All 12,544 two-call products are cross-checked by independent full coefficient convolution. The direct five-call word, all five call omissions, a mutated generator, the factor inverse law, group-table associativity, and a known two-call target control pass. `CERTIFICATE.json` records the two-call state digest `7313957379a9c51963604fae5f6a69edda1771006526c9c2ef4ab068e76bed95`.

The direct target costs five. A four-call factorization would reduce this finite model bill by 20%; the exact minimum remains five. The bit-model address labels have no priced implementation in the selected multiplication supplier, so this experiment yields no exponent change.

## Pins and overlap

Track `bit-mechanisms`; seed `592f04c45f93ecfac35ea0ab971b12ba`; task `bit-new-register-model`; priority revision 3; catalogue SHA-256 `6686ad58f1fbdbc87134a78901b60fd53a20d3984355e91defbbebc9e9fa8075`; exact research base `1c47876ef742ba64bf9140b0527d63acf656a3b4`; selected-record SHA-256 `10b9e340fd8e354a37a0c4813c90e5de1dd42044b5f6aca4a3fc5a42b685fa32`. The package pins the in-tree three-register abelian predecessor. The nearest nonabelian results are PR #1822 (head `ee736b4b11bbd63b04d94c8edafb3790161ebdea`, Q8 repeated central-commutator pair) and PR #1925 (head `009ed860f34ed5d7b0d626098ce93c4c2a7eb4df`, Q8 mixed targets); this scope changes the group to `SL2(F3)` and uses the heterogeneous `i,w,w^-1iw` endpoint. It imports no predecessor code. The exact-term overlap search found no separate `SL2(F3)` or binary-tetrahedral PR/claim.

The selected record remains the maintainer-reviewed conditional finite construction with `kappa = 836330098538459/500000000000000000`; its certificate and reproduction obligations are unchanged. The experiment does not invoke the selected-source cold replay.

## Verification and limits

- `python3 -I -O -B research/sl2f3-conjugate-triple-seed592f/verify.py` — passes on CPython 3.14.7.
- `python3 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/sl2f3-conjugate-triple-seed592f --check-only` — passes source pins and metadata.
- `git diff --check` — passes.

The package runner requests Python 3.12; it is not installed locally, so I did not run that wrapper. The direct exact verifier passes under the available interpreter. No proof-assistant formalization or physical source/hosting/precision/restoration budget is claimed. The result is limited to the named finite address group, alphabet, endpoint, and three roles.
